why: A profile with no CIF ID cannot be linked to accounts, KYC or AML screening.
Two rows for one CIF ID double-count customers and break every join on customer.

rule_name: BVN present for KYC tier 2 and 3
check: bvn is not null where kyc_tier >= 2
why: Tiered KYC requires identity verification above tier 1; a tier 2/3 customer with no BVN is a regulatory finding.
A malformed BVN fails NIBSS verification and silently defeats duplicate-identity checks.
A BVN on two CIFs is either a re-onboarded customer (split exposure, double counted) or identity misuse.

rule_name: Phone is a valid Nigerian mobile (after standardisation)
why: OTPs, transaction alerts and collections all go to this number.

rule_name: Phone captured in E.164 at source
why: Measures standardisation load; the fix is an input mask in the onboarding apps.

rule_name: State of residence is one of the 36 states or FCT
why: Drives regional reporting, agent coverage planning and AML geography risk scoring.

check: date_of_birth between (batch_as_of - interval 110 year)::date and (batch_as_of - interval 18 year)::date
why: Placeholder (1900-01-01), future and under-age birth dates break age-based KYC and product eligibility.
Email is optional on USSD and agent onboarding, so it is tracked against a tolerance, not zero defects.
Statements and e-receipts bounce.
Tier sets the transaction and balance limits enforced downstream.
Stale CIF data means new customers are missing from limits and AML screening.

rule_name: Customer file row count matches control total
why: A short file means customers are silently missing downstream.
Duplicate account rows fan out every join from transactions and double balances.
An account with no owner has no KYC tier, no AML profile and cannot be reported to regulators.

rule_name: Account number is a valid NUBAN (CBN check digit)
check: account_number is a 10-digit NUBAN with a valid CBN check digit
why: An invalid NUBAN cannot receive NIP inflows; funds sent to it are rejected or misrouted.

rule_name: Closure date present on closed accounts
check: closed_at is not null where status = 'CLOSED'
why: Without a closure date, post-closure activity controls (DQ-TXN-017) cannot run.
Status drives debit blocks, dormancy reporting and closure controls.
New accounts would appear as orphans in the transaction feed.

rule_name: Account file row count matches control total
why: A short file means accounts are silently missing downstream.
Terminal ID is the join key from every POS transaction to its agent.

rule_name: One device serial, one terminal ID
why: A device on two terminal IDs means a swap that was never retired; settlement can go to the old agent.
Cash-outs on this terminal cannot be settled to the agent.

rule_name: Terminal state is one of the 36 states or FCT
why: Agent network coverage and cash-logistics planning are done by state.
Newly activated terminals are missing, so their cash-outs fail the registry check.

rule_name: Terminal file row count matches control total
why: A short file means terminals are silently missing downstream.
Without an ID a transaction cannot be deduplicated, disputed or reconciled.
Repeated IDs inflate volume and value; silver keeps the latest version of each ID.
A transaction with no amount cannot be posted, settled or reported.
Direction carries the sign; zero or negative amounts double-reverse when summed.
Unknown status means we cannot tell whether money moved, so success rate and value are unreliable.

rule_name: Status sent in the canonical vocabulary at source
why: Measures standardisation load; the fix is a status mapping owned by each integration.

check: channel in (POS, TRANSFER, USSD, CARD, BILLS)
why: Channel drives fee rules, limits and every channel-level KPI.
Money moved against an account we do not hold; it cannot be attributed, limited or reconciled.
Cash-outs on unregistered terminals cannot be attributed to an agent for commission or fraud monitoring.

rule_name: POS transaction carries a terminal ID
check: terminal_id is not null where channel = 'POS'
why: A POS transaction with no terminal cannot be traced to an agent or a device.

rule_name: Transaction time between 2020 and the batch cut-off
check: created_at >= timestamp '2020-01-01' and created_at <= batch_as_of + interval 10 minute
why: 1970 and future-dated transactions land in the wrong reporting day, or no day at all.
Two ledger postings for one NIP session is a double debit; the customer has been charged twice.

rule_name: Transfer counterparty bank code is a known CBN code
check: counterparty_bank_code exists in ref_banks.bank_code where channel = 'TRANSFER'
why: Unknown bank codes break inter-bank settlement reporting and NIBSS reconciliation.
Negative settlement lag points at a timezone mismatch, which shifts transactions across settlement days.

rule_name: Fee not larger than the amount
why: Fee income is overstated and the customer may have been overcharged.

rule_name: Amount within the KYC tier single-transaction limit
why: Either a limit breach (compliance) or an amount in the wrong unit; both misstate value.

rule_name: No successful debits after account closure
check: not (account_status = 'CLOSED' and direction = 'DR' and status = 'SUCCESSFUL' and created_at > account_closed_at)
why: A debit on a closed account is a control failure (card not hot-listed) and a likely customer complaint.

check: coalesce(hours_since_last_load, 1e9) <= sla_hours where dataset = 'transactions' and partition_key = 'ALL'
why: Intraday liquidity, fraud and agent dashboards read this feed.

rule_name: Every transaction channel delivered within its SLA
check: coalesce(hours_since_last_load, 1e9) <= sla_hours where dataset = 'transactions' and partition_key <> 'ALL'
why: A dead channel is invisible to a table-level check while the other channels keep the max timestamp fresh.

rule_name: NIP transfer carries a session ID
check: session_id is not null where channel = 'TRANSFER'
why: The NIP session ID is the reference used for NIBSS reconciliation and customer disputes.
Separates true re-deliveries from legitimate status updates that share a transaction ID (DQ-TXN-002).

rule_name: Transaction file row count matches control total
why: Missing rows are missing money; every downstream total is understated with no visible error.
